sidecar_purpose: Repo-resident semantic image sidecar for the approved v1 compiled asset sheet of the Bit and Bot role kit. Supports role continuity, prompt constraint extraction, and asset cataloguing.
source_truth_note: This sidecar records the compiled sheet image. The repo image bytes and the package manifest remain authoritative for custody; this sidecar does not authorize derivative images or broaden canon beyond the observed panels.
runtime_use_note: Use this sidecar to locate the compiled role-kit reference and route it for character selection, prompt planning, and QA. It is not a sliced runtime sprite atlas.
do_not_infer_note: Do not infer unseen panels, extra roles, exact caption text, or color values beyond what is visible. Do not use this sidecar as a prompt or generation contract, and do not treat it as final acceptance of new art.

provenance.prompt_unretained_note: Exact prompt not retained. The sheet was compiled from the 12 bot-role-kit source PNGs listed in the package manifest using the Adventures of Patch asset-sheet compiler.

summary: Approved v1 compiled asset sheet for the Bit and Bot role kit. The sheet is compiled from the 12 source PNGs (chef, cowboy, detective, mechanic) and presents a four-column by three-row grid: the top row shows a full-figure hero pose for each role, and the two lower rows show alternate poses. A dark green document header and rules, a white background, and dark caption bars beneath each panel give the sheet its reference-sheet structure.

document_header: A dark green header bar occupies the top of the sheet.
The header contains the sheet title and role-kit guidance text in a light color.
Template status and source information are shown in the header area.
layout_grid: The sheet is arranged as a four-column by three-row grid of panels.
Each column corresponds to one role in the bot-role-kit (chef, cowboy, detective, mechanic).
A white background with dark green vertical and horizontal rules separates the panels.
hero_views: The top row of each column shows a full-figure hero pose for that role.
Each hero panel is the largest cell in its column.
Hero poses are centered and face the viewer with role-specific props or costume elements.
alternate_views: The middle and bottom rows of each column show alternate poses or actions for the same role.
Alternate panels are smaller than the hero panels but maintain the same column width.
The panels depict role-specific actions (e.g., mixing, lassoing, investigating, tooling).
panel_captions_and_rules: A dark caption bar appears beneath each panel, separated from the image by a thin rule.
Dark green vertical rules divide the four columns.
Dark green horizontal rules separate the header, rows, and the footer.
character_design: Bit and Bot are white-bodied, rounded support robots with wheeled bases and simple faces.
Neither character wears a teal hoodie, crossbody bag, Patch face panel, or Patch silhouette.
Role-specific costume pieces and props distinguish the panels without changing the base bot shape.
color_and_style: White and off-white dominate the background and margins.
Dark green rules and dark caption bars provide the template structure.
Role accents include blue, green, brown, and tan from hats, tools, and accessories.
The art style is clean, vector-like, and Patch-compatible while remaining non-Patch.

positive_constraints: Bit and Bot are a support-bot duo used in Patch Mission Control scenes and role-kit scenarios.
Preserve the four role columns in order: chef, cowboy, detective, and mechanic.
Preserve the three-row layout: one hero pose on top and two alternate poses below for each role.
Keep Bit and Bot clearly non-Patch: no hoodie, bag, Patch face panel, or Patch silhouette.
Use the hero and alternate panels as canonical references for role-specific poses and props.
Preserve the white background, dark green template rules, and dark caption bars.
Respect role-specific costume and prop identity (chef, cowboy, detective, mechanic).
negative_constraints: Do not depict Bit or Bot as human, organic, or wearing Patch-style clothing.
Do not add a Patch face panel, Patch bag, or Patch silhouette to either character.
Do not swap, remove, or rename the four role columns.
Do not infer exact caption wording beyond what is legible in the image.
Do not introduce backgrounds, textures, or lighting beyond the clean white reference style.
Do not treat this compiled sheet as a sliced runtime sprite atlas or animation specification.

best_for: Selecting hero and alternate poses for Bit and Bot in each role-kit role.
Prompt constraints for new Bit and Bot role-kit images.
QA of role-specific costume and prop identity.
Composing Mission Control or role-kit scenes with Bit and Bot.
not_sufficient_for: Final acceptance of derivative art without image QA.
Exact RGB color values or final shader treatment.
Animation frames, timing, or bone rigging not shown.
Using directly as a sliced runtime sprite atlas.
